title: Symphony of the day — research record
description: The scholarly record for one work. Upstream of data/works/<slug>.json: everything the card needs is in here, plus the provenance the card has no room for. scripts/research_to_work.py turns this into a prepare_work.py run.

slug.description: Matches data/works/<slug>.json. Convention: surname-noNN (beethoven-no-3), using the number even where the work has a famous nickname, so a composer's symphonies sort in order. The nickname goes in title_short. mozart-linz and shostakovich-leningrad predate the rule and keep their names.

researched.description: ISO date this record was compiled.

title_full.description: As it should read on the card, nickname in curly quotes.

title_short.description: Nickname alone, e.g. Linz. Empty if the work has none.

title_spoken.description: Override for the title as spoken in the reel script. Leave it out unless the derived one reads badly: the script drops the opus number and says the nickname as words, which handles most titles.

nationality.description: Adjectival, e.g. Austrian. Use the identity Grove uses; note contested or shifting cases in nationality_note.

nationality_note.description: For composers whose nationality is contested, changed, or anachronistic — e.g. a German born in a state that did not yet exist.

born_date.description: Birth date, ISO where possible: 1770-12-17. The reel script says the composer's age aloud, and subtracting years is a year too high for any work finished before the birthday, so record this wherever the sources give it. Where the birth itself is unrecorded and the sources give a baptism instead — Beethoven — record the baptism and say so in `unknowns`: it is the standard proxy and is never more than a few days out.

era.description: The scholarly judgment. data/periods.json buckets mechanically by year and drives the card colour; when the two disagree, say why in era_note and decide deliberately.

year.description: Single year for the card. For a work spanning years, the year of completion.

date.description: Finest known date, ISO where possible: 1783-11-04, 1783-11, autumn 1783.

country_then.description: The CONSTITUENT LAND at the time and nothing above it — Archduchy of Austria, Kingdom of Bohemia, Duchy of Styria, Austrian Silesia, Russian SFSR. Printed on card 2 under the place name, where it sits directly beneath a map already printing the sovereign state, so naming the sovereign here too (or appending it: 'Duchy of Styria, Austria-Hungary') just says it twice. Where the place had no land between it and the sovereign, leave it empty rather than repeating `polity`.

polity.description: THE COUNTRY OF COMPOSITION: the sovereign state the place belonged to in the year of composition, named as a historian would name it that year. This is the authoritative one — it is printed on the map and is the label the card shows, so it must be fact-checked against Grove like any other field and must appear in `claims`. Distinct from country_then, which may name a constituent duchy or kingdom (Archduchy of Austria) rather than the sovereign entity above it (Habsburg Monarchy). Watch the anachronisms: no Austrian Empire before August 1804, no Austria-Hungary before 1867, no Italy or Germany before 1861 and 1871. Keep it short enough to print — over about 34 characters it wraps to a third line on the card.

polity_note.description: Why this polity and not another: a contested case, a succession in the year of composition, or a place whose sovereign changed between the sketches and the finished work.

note.description: For works written in more than one place, or where the attribution is disputed.

lat.description: Verified latitude. Pin it here: prepare_work.py geocodes the place NAME through a Wikidata search, and a bare city name resolves to the wrong continent often enough to matter (Vienna finds Vienna, Illinois). Set lat/lon and the build stops guessing.

wikidata.description: Q-id the coordinates came from, so the next person can check rather than re-search.

completed.description: The finest known date the work was FINISHED, where `date` is a span and cannot say: 1802-10, 'summer 1802'. Used only to date the composer's age in the reel script, which is otherwise ambiguous by a year for a work written across a birthday.

summary.description: Card 2's occasion line. Aim for 90 characters or fewer; 148 is the observed ceiling before the type shrinks past comfort.

dedicatee.description: Often not the patron. Record both when they differ.

occasion_spoken.description: The same fact as `occasion`, worded to be spoken: it has to follow "composed in <year> for" in the reel script and read as one sentence. "a benefit concert of his own", not "A benefit concert for the composer." No full stop. Without it the script reads `occasion` verbatim and warns.

commission.description: Fee, terms, or the absence of a commission where that is the interesting fact.

detail.description: The long version, for the Obsidian note.

known.description: false when the premiere is unrecorded or disputed — then say so in notes rather than guessing.

venue_short.description: The venue as the card should print it, where the scholarly name carries a parenthetical or an alternative title. Omit and the card uses venue verbatim.

scoring.description: What it takes to play the work, for card 2's first fact. Three DIFFERENT questions live here, and the card answers whichever is best attested — in this order: what the composer specified, then who actually played it, then what the score's parts add up to. Record every one you can source; research_to_work.py applies the priority and picks the card's label to match, so the card never implies a stronger claim than the source supports. There is deliberately no 'modern complement' option: a present-day string section is a convention of ours, not a fact about the work, and this series prints the period fact or nothing — the same rule as composition.place.polity.

specified.description: FIRST PRIORITY. Player counts the composer wrote INTO the score — '16 first violins', not an editor's guess. Rare before the late romantics, and the strongest thing the card can say. Card label: SCORED FOR.

players.description: Total players the composer asked for.

note.description: Where in the score the numbers appear.

source.description: id of the entry in `sources` that carries it.

premiere.description: SECOND PRIORITY. How many people were on the platform on the night, where the roster is documented. A fact about an event, not about the work, which is why the card labels it PREMIERE ORCHESTRA rather than SCORED FOR.

strings.description: Documented string numbers, e.g. '24 violins, 10 violas, 12 cellos and basses'.

note.description: Whose account this is. Premiere rosters are usually reported second-hand and often disagree.

source.description: id of the entry in `sources` that carries it.

instrumentation.description: THIRD PRIORITY, and the usual case. What the score's parts add up to: the instruments called for, counting a doubling player ONCE. It cannot give a player total, because string numbers are almost never in the score — so the card says '67 instruments', not '67 players'. Card label: SCORED FOR.

instruments.description: Instruments the score calls for. Doublings counted once.

shorthand.description: The publisher's shorthand verbatim, e.g. '3.2.2.3 - 2.2.3.0 - timp - strings'.

doublings.description: What the doublings are, e.g. 'two of the four flutes take piccolo'.

note.description: How the count was arrived at.

source.description: id of the entry in `sources` that carries it.

voices.description: Singers, where the work needs them. Never folded into any players total: a chorus is a different kind of force and the card names it separately.

source.description: id of the entry in `sources` that carries it.

line.description: Override for the card's fact text. Leave out and research_to_work.py derives it from whichever block won the priority.

label.description: Override for the card's label. Leave out and the winning block picks it. Only these two exist.

hook.description: One sentence a viewer who has never heard the piece can act on. 64–71 characters is the range that sits well on the card.

spoken.description: The card hook worded to be spoken: it has to follow "Listen out for" in the reel script. "four notes, and a whole first movement built from almost nothing else", not "Four notes. The whole first movement is built from almost nothing else." No full stop. Only the hook flagged `card` needs one.

detail.description: The long version, for the Obsidian note.

timing.description: Movement and roughly where in it, e.g. IV, from the first bar.

card.description: Exactly one entry should be true — the hook that goes on the card.

id.description: Short handle used in claims, e.g. grove-mozart.

container.description: Grove Music Online, The Musical Times …

zotero_key.description: Filled in once saved to the Symphony of the day collection.

snapshot.description: Zotero attachment key of the stored copy of the page as consulted. Expected on every `grove` source: Grove sits behind the Sydney University login and Oxford revises articles in place, so the URL alone proves nothing later. See scripts/grove_snapshot.py.

claims.description: Provenance per field: dotted path -> list of source ids. Every field that reaches the card must appear here. Two ids means Grove and Wikipedia agree.

conflicts.description: Where the sources disagreed, and what was done about it. An empty array means checked and clean, not unchecked.

unknowns.description: Things genuinely not known, stated as such. Better here than silently absent.

obsidian_note.description: Vault-relative path of the human-readable note.
